newsitem.title: CHILE: SOCCER-SALAS SCORES HAT-TRICK AS CHILE BEAT COLOMBIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SALAS SCORES HAT-TRICK AS CHILE BEAT COLOMBIA.

text.p: Marcelo Salas scored a first-half hat-trick as Chile thrashed faltering Colombia 4-1 in a World Cup qualifier Saturday.

Salas gave Chile a 3-0 halftime lead, Hamilton Ricard pulled one back for Colombia early in the second half and striker Ivan Zamorano completed the scoring with a 90th-minute penalty, his 10th goal of the qualifying tournament.

Chile moved into fourth place in the single South American group with 16 points from 11 games, although they could be overtaken Sunday when Bolivia and Ecuador, who are two points below them, play away to Peru and Venezuela respectively.
Colombia remained third with 18 points from 12 games but have faded badly, having taken only one point in their last five matches. The top four teams qualify for the World Cup in France.
Colombia recalled their top players, who had been rested during the Copa America last month, but were overrun in the first half as playmaker Carlos Valderrama was marked out of the game.
Marcelo Vega gave hint of what was to come when he struck the Colombian post after less than one minute before Salas, who plays for Argentina's River Plate, scored with a header in the 16th minute.
Salas increased the lead 10 minutes later, steering Zamorano's wayward shot into the goal, and completed his hat-trick four minutes before halftime, heading in a cross by the same player.
Colombia were a new team after the break, especially when Ricard, one of two players brought on at halftime, scored in the 52nd minute.
Valderrama began to look more like his old self and Colombia had the ball in the net again two minutes from time, but the goal was controversially disallowed.
Two minutes later the Colombians felt wronged again when Chile were awarded the penalty from which Zamorano completed the scoring.
Chile play four of their last five games at home, where they have a 100 percent record.
